answer: Last night a thousand shell accounts flooded a grant vote — a trellis of votes propped by one bot farmer. Slashable stake cuts it down: each identity locks 500 POA in kernel escrow thawing only after three clean closes, and one duplication proof — the same device fingerprint on two identities — burns the whole bond, not a fraction. Fielding 1,000 fakes locks 500,000 POA, all risked on one proof. This defeats clone-army voting, where numbers used to win. The trade-off: newcomers without capital are screened out, and weight tilts toward holders who can afford a timber yard of bonds.
